theory_refs.at: Inner skip loops also check l < r

stages.title: Understand
stages.body:
✍️ f(string) → true if, after dropping non-alphanumeric characters and ignoring case, it reads the same both ways.
- Length ≤ 2·10⁵, printable ASCII.
- "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama" → true.

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body:
✍️ By hand: compare the first letter with the last, skipping spaces and punctuation, moving inwards.
✍️ Hard part: skipping on both sides without running past each other.
✍️ Edges: empty after cleaning (e.g. " ", ".,") → true; "0P" → false (digits count).

stages.title: Brainstorm: brute → optimal
stages.body:
✍️ **1. Simple.** Build a cleaned lowercase copy, compare it with its reverse. O(n) time, O(n) space. Perfectly acceptable as a first answer.
✍️ ↳ The extra string is the only cost; the follow-up asks for O(1) space.
✍️ **2. Optimal.** Two pointers on the original string, skipping non-alphanumerics on each side, comparing lowercase forms. O(n), O(1).

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body:
✍️ 1. l at the start, r at the end.
✍️ 2. Move l right past non-alphanumeric characters; move r left likewise (never crossing).
✍️ 3. If the lowercase characters differ, return false; else move both inwards.
✍️ 4. If the pointers meet, return true.

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
STATE   l = 0; r = n-1
LOOP    while l < r
UPDATE    while l < r and not alnum(s[l]): l++
          while l < r and not alnum(s[r]): r--
CHECK     if lower(s[l]) != lower(s[r]): return false
UPDATE    l++; r--
RETURN  true
```

stages.title: Reference Java
Dry run
stages.body:
"race a car" → cleaned "raceacar":
| l char | r char | equal? |
|---|---|---|
| r | r | yes |
| a | a | yes |
| c | c | yes |
| e | a | no → false |

stages.title: Edge cases and complexity
stages.body:
✍️ O(n) time, O(1) space.
✍️ All non-alphanumeric → the inner loops stop at l == r → returns true.
- `tolower` on digits leaves them unchanged.

stages.title: Carry forward
stages.body:
✍️ Palindrome / symmetry → opposite ends, compare, move both.
✍️ Any inner skip loop must repeat the outer guard (`l < r`).

stages.title: Interview follow-ups
stages.body:
- *Allow deleting one character* (LeetCode 680): at the first mismatch, try skipping either side ([[str-palindrome-checks#one-deletion]]).
- *Longest palindromic substring* — expand around centers (Day 8).

siblings.title: Valid Palindrome II
siblings.maps: At the first mismatch you get one deletion: try skipping the left char or the right char.

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body:
✍️ Can the string be a palindrome after deleting at most one character?
✍️ Brute: delete each position and check → O(n²).

stages.title: Brainstorm
stages.body: ✍️ Before the first mismatch everything matched, so the deletion must be one of the two mismatching characters. Check s[l+1..r] or s[l..r−1] → O(n).

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body: ✍️ Walk inwards; on a mismatch return isPal(l+1, r) || isPal(l, r−1); if no mismatch, true.

stages.title: Pseudocode
Reference Java
Quick theory
stages.body: ✍️ "At most one mistake allowed" → handle the first mistake both possible ways, then continue normally ([[str-palindrome-checks#one-deletion]]).

siblings.title: Reverse Vowels of a String
siblings.maps: Opposite ends that only stop on vowels — same skip-loop structure as Valid Palindrome.

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body: ✍️ Reverse only the vowels (both cases) of a string.

stages.title: Brainstorm
stages.body: ✍️ Move l to the next vowel, r to the previous vowel, swap, repeat.

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body: ✍️ Skip non-vowels on both sides (guarding l < r), swap, move inwards.

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
while l < r:
    while l < r and not vowel(s[l]): l++
    while l < r and not vowel(s[r]): r--
    swap(s[l++], s[r--])
```

stages.title: Reference Java
Quick theory
stages.body: ✍️ The skip-loop structure is reusable for any "act only on some characters" two-pointer problem.

siblings.title: Reverse Only Letters
siblings.maps: Identical shape with `isalpha` as the filter.

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body: ✍️ Reverse the letters, leaving every non-letter in place.

stages.title: Brainstorm
stages.body: ✍️ Opposite ends skipping non-letters; swap letters.

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body: ✍️ Same as reverse vowels with the filter "is a letter".

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
while l < r: skip non-letters on both sides; swap; move inwards
```

stages.title: Reference Java
Quick theory
stages.body: ✍️ Pattern recognition: if two problems differ only in the filter predicate, they are the same problem.
